buildCommand: npm run build --workspace=packages/shared && npm run build --workspace=apps/web
$comment_rewrites: The SPA fallback deliberately does NOT cover /assets/ or /theme-bootstrap.js. It used to be a bare /(.*) catch-all, which is what turned a missing hashed asset into 'Refused to apply style ... MIME type (text/html)': the request for a stale /assets/index-<hash>.css found no file, fell through to the rewrite, and was answered with index.html under Content-Type: text/html. Excluding them means a file that is not deployed returns an honest 404 the browser can recover from, instead of HTML pretending to be a script or a stylesheet — which for the theme bootstrap would be a syntax error in <head> on every page rather than a missing style. Everything else still falls through, so client-side routes keep working.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.blood.aspireshield.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.$comment: Vite content-hashes every filename under /assets, so a given URL's bytes never change. Caching them forever is what makes a deploy cheap; the hash changing is the cache bust.

index.html is the one file that must never be served stale: it is the document that names which asset hashes exist. A cached copy from a previous deploy is precisely how a browser ends up asking for a hash that was removed — the other half of the MIME-type failure above. no-cache means revalidate every time, not 'do not store'.

The theme bootstrap is not content-hashed — it is referenced by a fixed path from index.html, which is the only way it can run before the bundle exists. Unhashed means it must revalidate, for the same reason index.html does: a cached copy from a previous deploy is a stale copy with nothing to bust it.
